justloaddata<-1

### SPLITTING LONGER TEXTS INTO SHORTER ONES
  
data$idl<-seq(1:length(data$ID))

splitSentence <- function(sentence, blockLength) {
   words <- strsplit(sentence, " ")[[1]]
   blocks <- c()
   currentBlock <- ""
   for (i in 1:length(words)) {
      word <- words[i]
      if (wordcount(currentBlock) + wordcount(word) <= blockLength) {
         currentBlock <- paste(currentBlock, word, sep = " ")
      } else {
         blocks <- c(blocks, currentBlock)
         currentBlock <- word
      }
   }
   if (wordcount(currentBlock) > 0) {
      blocks <- c(blocks, currentBlock)
   }
   return(blocks)
}


#print(result)
data<-as.data.frame(data)

blockLength <- 300
data_split<-data
istr_num<-1
i_num<-1
counter<-c()
for (istr in 1:length(data$idl)){
  sentence <- data$txt_clean[istr]
  result <- splitSentence(sentence, blockLength)
  istr_num<-length(result)
  
  data_split[i_num:(i_num+istr_num-1),]<-as.data.frame(lapply(data[istr,], rep, istr_num))
  # for (iii in i_num:(i_num+istr_num-1)){
  # data_lemmatized_split[iii,]<-data_lemmatized[istr,]
  # }
  data_split$txt_clean[i_num:(i_num+istr_num-1)]<-result
  i_num<-i_num+istr_num
  counter<-c(counter, istr_num)
  print(c(istr,istr_num))
}
max(counter)

Here we observe:

 - the figure with topic proportions, i.e. how much text explained by each of the topics;  
 - the figure with topic summary printing 20 most frequent and exclusive words for each topic;  
 - summary of each topic with words having  highest probability (most frequent), frequency and exclusivity (FREX), LIFT and SCORE you can ignore as those are rather internal measures without intuitive interpretation;  
  - 5 representative responses for each topic ("representative" responses are sometimes very heterogeneous, but one should remember  that as we have many topics, most of responses consist of 2-3 topics (even the most representative ones!) so it is important to look on the exclusive words and wordclouds to get a better picture.)

  theta_subset <- ncpPrevFit_startup$theta[which(out2$meta$Year==year_id),]
   
  if (is.null(dim(theta_subset))) {
    # Single row: convert to 1-row matrix
    topic_year_share[year_idd,] <- ncpPrevFit_startup$theta[which(out2$meta$Year==year_id),]
   } else{
  
topic_year_share[year_idd,]<-colSums(ncpPrevFit_startup$theta[which(out2$meta$Year==year_id),])/sum(ncpPrevFit_startup$theta[which(out2$meta$Year==year_id),])
}
  
year_idd<-year_idd+1
}

#rowSums(topic_year_share)
topic_year_share<-as.data.frame(topic_year_share)
rownames(topic_year_share)<-years
colnames(topic_year_share)<-tiopiclabel
pdf("topic_year_share.pdf", width = 8, height = 8)  
par(mfrow = c(3, 3) ,mar=c(2,2,1,1))
for(k_i in Korder){
  matplot(rownames(topic_year_share), topic_year_share[,k_i], type='l', lty=1,lwd=2, xlab='Years', ylab='Share', col=col[k_i],xaxt='n',ylim=c(0,0.7))
  axis(side=1, at=unique(data$Year), labels=years)
  fit <- lm(topic_year_share[,k_i] ~ years)
  pred <- predict(fit, newdata = data.frame(years = years),
                interval = "confidence", level = 0.95)
  abline(fit, col = col[k_i], lwd = 1, lty = 1)
  lines(years, pred[, "lwr"], col = col[k_i], lty = 2)
  lines(years, pred[, "upr"], col = col[k_i], lty = 2)
  legend('topright', inset=.05, legend=colnames(topic_year_share)[k_i],pch=3, col=col[k_i])
}
dev.off()

```{r, echo=FALSE}
pdf("corr_plot.pdf", width = 8, height = 8) 
data_sentiment<-fread("Topic_prop_v3.5.csv")
X_vars <- data_sentiment[, c(18, 19, 20, 21, 22, 23, 24, 25, 26)] 
Y_vars <- data_sentiment[, c(27, 28, 29)] 
TopicCorrMatrix1 <- cor(X_vars, Y_vars)
rownames(TopicCorrMatrix1) <- colnames(X_vars)
colnames(TopicCorrMatrix1) <- colnames(Y_vars)
cor.mtest <- function(mat1, mat2){
  mat1 <- as.data.frame(mat1)
  mat2 <- as.data.frame(mat2)
  
  n1 <- ncol(mat1)
  n2 <- ncol(mat2)
  
  corr.mat <- matrix(NA, nrow = n1, ncol = n2)  # correlation values
  p.mat <- matrix(NA, nrow = n1, ncol = n2)     # p-values
  
  for(i in 1:n1){
    for(j in 1:n2){
      ans <- cor.test(mat1[[i]], mat2[[j]])
      corr.mat[i, j] <- ans$estimate   # correlation coefficient
      p.mat[i, j] <- ans$p.value       # p-value
    }
  }
  
  rownames(corr.mat) <- colnames(mat1)
  colnames(corr.mat) <- colnames(mat2)
  rownames(p.mat) <- colnames(mat1)
  colnames(p.mat) <- colnames(mat2)
  
  return(list(cor = corr.mat, p = p.mat))
}
result1 <- cor.mtest(X_vars, Y_vars)

corrplot(result1$cor, 
         is.corr = FALSE, 
         method = "square",
         tl.cex = 1.2,
         tl.col = "black",
         col.lim = c(-1, 1),
         cl.ratio = 0.9,
         col = colorRampPalette(c("blue", "white", "red"))(200),
         p.mat = result1$p,
         insig = "label_sig",
         sig.level = c(.01, .05, .10),
         pch.cex = 0.9,
         pch.col = "white")
dev.off()
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}

ctrls <- c("GDPreal", "FDI", "Inflation_yoy")

# make a copy of the STM data used for estimateEffect
meta_z <- out$meta

# z-score controls (mean 0, sd 1)
meta_z[ctrls] <- lapply(meta_z[ctrls], function(x) as.numeric(scale(x)))

# re-fit estimateEffect using the standardized meta
prep_z <- estimateEffect(
  Korder ~ GDPreal + FDI + Inflation_yoy + Tokayev,
  ncpPrevFit_startup,
  meta = meta_z,
  uncertainty = "Global"
)

summary(prep_z)
